Congratulations to the West Baltimore communities and leaders receiving $4.1 million in community grants tied to the Amtrak Frederick Douglass Tunnel Program. The Tunnel represents a historic federal investment in Baltimore, replacing the 153-year-old B&P Tunnel, rebuilding the West Baltimore MARC station, improving surrounding infrastructure and supporting thousands of jobs. Over ten years, the program will distribute $50 million in grants.

I worked with my colleagues in Congress to help secure this investment and press for protections, mitigation measures and community safeguards for the people who live along the project corridor. As construction moves forward, that Congressional oversight will continue so Baltimore receives the full protections and benefits of this federal investment.

I send my deepest appreciation to Principal Kimberly Hill at Mary Ann Winterling Elementary School for hosting the announcement. Kudos to Luigi Rosa, who leads the project for Amtrak, and to State Senator Antonio Hayes, Councilmen John Bullock and Jermaine Jones, and Comptroller Bill Henry for your work to ensure our constituents take advantage of this federal opportunity.

#FrederickDouglassTunnel #WestBaltimore #Baltimore #FederalInvestment #CommunityInvestment #Infrastructure #Amtrak #Maryland

It was an honor to visit Western High School at the Northwestern Building as Baltimore welcomed His Royal Highness Prince Edward, the Duke of Edinburgh, and celebrated seven Baltimore City high schools joining the Duke’s International Award program.

The program will give students opportunities to build skills, serve their communities and take on new challenges. Participating schools are Western High School, Baltimore City College, Baltimore Polytechnic Institute, Carver Vocational-Technical High School, Forest Park High School, Frederick Douglass High School, and the Academy for College and Career Exploration (ACCE).

I am grateful to the Duke, Baltimore City Schools CEO Dr. Jermaine Dawson, Maryland State Superintendent Dr. Carey Wright, and all who made this opportunity possible. Baltimore students deserve every opportunity to lead, serve, grow and create bigger futures for themselves

Congratulations to Safe Streets Belvedere on 379 consecutive days without a homicide. That is more than a statistic. It represents lives saved, families kept whole, and a community proving that violence is not inevitable. This milestone belongs to everyone doing the work: the violence interrupters, Mayor Scott and his team, MONSE, LifeBridge Health’s Center for Hope, law enforcement, prosecutors, community and faith organizations, and most importantly, the neighbors who call this community home. It takes an all-of-the-above approach: prevention, intervention, accountability, opportunity, treatment, federal investment, and neighbors looking out for one another.

Baltimore’s legacy is bigger than the violence others too often use to define us. Our story is one of people caring for one another, building neighborhoods, and refusing to give up on each other. Celebrate this moment, but don’t stop. Keep working. Keep believing in Baltimore. And most of all, keep loving one another. Congratulations, Safe Streets Belvedere. 379 days and counting.
🔗: https://t.co/qTR6RFTnRh

I’m proud to be an original co-sponsor of the Stem Cell Therapeutic and Research Reauthorization Act of 2025.

Advancing stem cell research and strengthening access to lifesaving bone marrow and cord blood transplants can provide hope to thousands of patients and families facing serious diseases.

I’m proud to support this bipartisan effort and will continue working to advance medical research that can heal people and save lives.

The theme for the Congressional Black Caucus Foundation’s 55th Annual Legislative Conference (ALC) was "Rooted, Ready, & Rising". I participated in five days of strategic programming and signature events, including the Day of Healing Prayer Breakfast and the Annual Phoenix Awards Dinner. #CBCF #ALC55 #CBCFALC #AnnualLegislativeConference

It's disgraceful that the Trump Administration is putting warning signs outside the National Museum of American History telling visitors that the truth inside cannot be trusted. I am proud to co-lead legislation with @rep_jackson and @Rep_Stansbury to cut off every federal dollar for this propaganda. Not one cent should pay for the government to slap a warning label on Black history, on Native history, on the parts of our past this President would rather bury.

Today at the National Museum of African American History and Culture, I joined with Congresspersons Jonathan Jackson and Melanie Stansbury, Bishop William J. Barber II, Pastor Robert Turner, other faith leaders, advocates gathered again for a call to action. Our message to the Trump administration was clear, and it centered on protecting the Smithsonian Museum and the full and honest telling of American history.

That history should not be under attack because its truths are difficult or inconvenient. Preserving it requires vigilance, commitment and a willingness to speak up when the record is being diminished or erased.

Without reservation our history must be preserved, protected and told truthfully.

And for those who need a reminder: If you attempt to erase it, we will replace it!"

#HandsOffOurHistory #AmericanHistory
#Smithsonian
#CBC

25 years ago today, Americans stood paralyzed as we watched 2,753 people in New York City, 184 people at The Pentagon, 40 people in Shanksville, PA, and 246 passengers and crew lose their lives at the hands of terrorist murderers who sought to destroy us at our core. First responders, firefighters, police officers, public safety workers, and everyday heroes risked their lives to rescue and save as many people as possible. Today, we stand united together in our mourning over the tremendous loss of human life. #911 #NeverForget #911Memorial #Remembering911

Last week, I co-led a letter with @RepWesleyBellMO, @RepStricklandWA and 70 colleagues to Secretary Hegseth and acting-Secretary of the Navy Hung Cao opposing any effort to rename the future USS Doris Miller after President Trump.

Doris “Dorie” Miller was an American hero who displayed extraordinary courage at Pearl Harbor and became the first Black American awarded the Navy Cross. Naming an aircraft carrier in his honor recognizes a legacy of service, sacrifice, and bravery that belongs in our nation’s history.

https://t.co/9w9x6w6HM1

#OnThisDay in 1963, the March on Washington for Jobs and Freedom brought more than 250,000 people to the nation’s capital to protest racial discrimination and show support for civil rights legislation pending in Congress. Rev. Dr. Martin Luther King Jr.'s famous “I Have a Dream” speech became a defining moment in the American civil rights movement. Today, we find ourselves defending the right to vote, fighting against setbacks and attacks on the Voting Rights Act. We must continue the fight to make sure every American citizen has equal access to the ballot box. #VotingRights #ProtectTheVote #DefendTheVote #MarchOnWashington #liberty #justice #freedom

Reps. Kweisi Mfume (D-MD) and Chris Smith (R-NJ) have announced that they will be co-chairing the new, bipartisan Frederick Douglass Trafficking Victims Protection and Prevention Caucus in the U.S. House of Representatives.
